 Waiver Granted Pursuant to Section 39
 In accordance with section 39 of the Conflict of Interest Act, Mr. Yves Giroux, Parliamentary Budget Officer, has been granted a waiver of his limitation period under section 36 to enable him to accept a short-term contract with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). 
Mr. Giroux applied for a waiver of the period that applies to former reporting public office holders for one year following their last day in office. The waiver allows Mr. Giroux to accept a short-term contract with the OECD. 
In reviewing Mr. Giroux’s request, I considered all relevant factors listed under subsection 39(3) of the Act, which include the following: 
- the circumstances under which the reporting public office holder left his or her office: 
Mr. Giroux’s seven-year mandate ends September 2, 2025.
- the nature, and significance to the Government of Canada, of information possessed by the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder by virtue of that office holder’s public office;
The contract with the OECD does not require the use of confidential or material information in order to be carried out.
- the degree to which the new employer might gain unfair commercial advantage by hiring the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder: 
The OECD is an international organization which does not have a commercial purpose. The OECD aims to promote cooperation and benefits all its members, including Canada. Mr. Giroux’s contract would not provide the OECD an unfair commercial advantage.
- the authority and influence possessed by the reporting public office holder or former reporting public office holder while in public office:
The Office of the Parliamentary Budget Officer is recognized for its expertise and Mr. Giroux’s contract with the OECD would serve the public interest by allowing Canada’s expertise to be shared with other partner countries.
In light of the above, I have determined that the public interest in granting the waiver in relation to Mr. Giroux’s short-term contract with the OECD outweighs the public interest in maintaining the prohibition. I have therefore waived the limitation period.
All other post-employment obligations under the Act continue to apply, including the prohibition on contracting or accepting employment or an appointment to a board position with any other entity set out in subsection 35(1) as well as the prohibition on making representations within the meaning of subsection 35(2), for the duration of Mr. Giroux’s limitation period.
